rapport_notes: Joanna is genuinely warm, patient with Gabriel's lengthy logistics discussion, and builds trust through validation and clear explanations.
process_discipline_notes: No silence held after 'Does that make sense?' — Joanna immediately continues with the next pitch without letting the customer respond.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'So in order for us to give you a personalized estimate just need to ask you some about this move of course.' — framing present but time-boxed ask and promise are soft/implicit rather than explicit.
evidence_quotes.agenda: Joanna: 'And yeah, if you have any do you have any major concerns about moving in general or about this move that you want us to discuss as well?' — asked before logistics probing begins.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Gabriel raises concern about the solid wood king bedroom set being heavy and difficult to move. Joanna responds 'Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Oh, it is? Okay, solid wood. Oh, yeah, okay.' and Gabriel elaborates further. Gabriel also raises concern about washer/dryer stands being fragile; Joanna asks 'is it gas or just an electric' and Gabriel explains the disconnection and careful handling needed. Joanna acknowledges: 'Mm-hmm. Of course of course. Mm-hmm. Of course.' and validates his expertise.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Joanna: 'First is our no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.' — delivered in Stage 2 (not raised as a concern in Stage 1, so rightfully placed as a differentiator).
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Joanna: 'Second is meet your mover feature rest assured Gabriel, we don't take daily. Contract the workers, our guys are the most wedded movers in the industry and we send you their names ahead of time to let you know who's coming to help out with the move.' — delivered in Stage 2.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Joanna: 'And lastly on time guarantee if we run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts by the end of the day.' — delivered in Stage 2.
evidence_quotes.communication: Joanna: 'We will only start the time once we arrive at the pickup location and open the contract for you.' This is operational clarity but not the explicit 'day-before call, named crew lead, inbox updates' communication differentiator. Not fully covered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'Typically a house this size usually take six and a half to eight and a half hours to complete with three guys. Again this is just because of the typical square footage.' — gives range and personalizes to the house size and item volume mentioned.
evidence_quotes.estimate_window: Joanna: 'If you are available for a virtual walk through like the video call we can do that at your convenience and or send us a complete inventory list or photos 60 for you of everything we're moving for you that way we will just adjust the estimates based on the items we're doing, we're moving so far.' — communicates that estimate adjusts based on actual inventory.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Joanna: 'Once we hit the minimum, we only charge in every fifteen minutes after the minimum is mat.' — implies pay-less-if-faster structure.
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Joanna: 'So, basically, the more items you try to move yourself, you know, the lesser, the time, the shorter the move the lower the cost.' — clear self-prep cost benefit.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Joanna: 'in case you are already ready to go ahead with the booking all you have to do is give us the date, we'll check it for you and then we don't take deposits so there's no rain securing a spot.' — implies rate locks on booking, though not explicitly stated as 'rate locks when you book.'
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: Joanna does not deliver a clear 'would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent explicit close ask. The conversation ends with 'Alright, thank you and I'll send you that quote and I'll send you a text message with the link where you can join tomorrow' — which is a walkthrough scheduling handoff but lacks an explicit commitment ask.

top_strength: Joanna expertly navigated a complex, logistics-heavy intake call by asking the agenda question early, following up on customer concerns about heavy/fragile items with validation, and delivering all four key differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and self-prep cost savings) in a natural flow rather than as a mechanical checklist.
coaching_note: Hold silence after open-ended questions ('Does that make sense?') to give Gabriel space to respond or ask clarifying questions before moving forward, and add an explicit close ask ('Would you like to move forward with our help?') even on walkthrough-routed calls to confirm willingness before handing off to the video call scheduler.
